# SHA-256 digests of the build dependencies the Windows workflow downloads.
#
# Everything listed here ends up inside artifacts this project Authenticode-
# signs, and every one of them is fetched from a release asset over the
# network. TLS proves who served the bytes, not what the bytes are: a
# compromised or re-uploaded upstream asset arrives under a valid certificate
# and would be signed and shipped without anyone noticing. A digest committed
# here makes changing what the build consumes a reviewable change to this file.
#
# Format, one dependency per line, whitespace-separated:
#
#   <name> <version> <sha256|commit|unrecorded> [# comment]
#
# A 64-hex value is the SHA-256 of the downloaded file, checked by
# .github/scripts/verify-checksum.sh. A 40-hex value is a git commit id, for a
# dependency the build clones rather than downloads, checked by
# .github/scripts/verify-commit.sh - a tag is a movable pointer, the commit is
# not.
#
# `unrecorded` means the value for that version has not been captured yet: the
# build warns and continues. A *missing* line fails the build, so bumping a
# version cannot silently skip verification.
#
# To record one, on a machine that can reach the upstream host:
#
#   curl -sSfL <the exact url the action downloads> -o dep.bin
#   sha256sum dep.bin
#
# and paste the digest in place of `unrecorded`. Cross-check it against the
# upstream project's own published checksum or signature where one exists
# (OpenSSL and Lua publish both) - re-hashing whatever the download happens to
# return only records what you were served, which is not the same as verifying
# it.
#
# name          version   sha256 or commit

# Downloaded release assets, verified by sha256.
#
# openssl was cross-checked against the .sha256 OpenSSL publishes next to the
# asset. protobuf, cryptopp and miniz publish no checksum of their own, so the
# digests here record the bytes a fetch returned; they still turn a later
# substitution of the asset into a build failure, which is what this file is
# for.
openssl         3.5.9     603f5602e2eef00d77fbd429d34dcd5822bb301757a1bc9cdb24c670f1eb859a  # matches the upstream openssl-3.5.9.tar.gz.sha256
protobuf        21.12     29b0f6b6d5714f212b8549cd0cb6fc531672630e41fb99d445421bc4d1bbb9cd
cryptopp        8.9.0     4cc0ccc324625b80b695fcd3dee63a66f1a460d3e51b71640cdbfc4cd1a3779c
miniz           3.1.1     cb28402bb2af93bdc331b60d16807e89727d1712a2d0a7ba0cac79a3e406fe40

# boost_1_86_0.tar.gz, fetched and verified by .github/actions/boost for
# every Windows build (x86, x64, ARM64 and legacy XP). The digest is the
# SHA256 the Boost 1.86.0 release page publishes for the .tar.gz, compared
# against that page by hand. It was also cross-checked independently: the
# .tar.bz2 of the same release matches the digest conan-center-index records
# for it, and both archives decompress to the same tar.
boost           1.86.0    2575e74ffc3ef1cd0babac2c1ee8bdb5782a0ee672b1912da40e5b4b591ca01f  # matches the Boost 1.86.0 release page

# lua-5.4.8.tar.gz from www.lua.org. The digest is the checksum lua.org
# publishes for it, compared against that page by hand. It was also
# cross-checked independently: the tarball is byte-identical to the
# Debian/Ubuntu lua5.4_5.4.8.orig.tar.gz, whose .dsc records the same SHA-256,
# and conan-center-index records the same digest for the lua.org URL.
lua             5.4.8     4f18ddae154e793e46eeab727c59ef1c0c0c2b744e7b94219710d76f530629ae  # matches the lua.org download page

# Cloned, not downloaded, and pinned to the commit rather than the tag.
#
# These used to be fetched as the zip/tar.gz GitHub generates for a tag. That
# archive is not a release artifact anybody signs, and the tag it is generated
# from can be moved; the commit cannot. Recording the commit and cloning at the
# tag verifies the same thing a digest would, without depending on an archive
# whose bytes are a server-side product. Each value is the commit the tag
# resolves to (annotated tags peeled: mariadb's v3.4.9 tag object is
# cc4d78c4..., the commit it points at is the one below).
googletest      1.12.1    58d77fa8070e8cec2dc1ed015d66b454c8d78850
tinyxml2        10.1.0    57eea48c5bfc354ac45d53b2eb499e66c80d63e0
mongoose        7.24      91b87a6bd8568f101680d4fc0db3d8773f74eb6c
mariadb         3.4.9     64e9fe09fea6a017bab92e19a08d2301e3da5b56

# check_nsclient, from https://github.com/mickem/check_nsclient/releases,
# keyed by the version in .check_nsclient_version. Each release publishes a
# SHA256SUMS over its binaries and their CycloneDX SBOMs, and attests every
# binary, the SBOM of each, and the SHA256SUMS itself from its release
# workflow. The digests below are the ones in that SHA256SUMS, and the
# attestations were verified before recording them: all name
# .github/workflows/release.yml of mickem/check_nsclient at commit 0870385
# (the 1.2.0 tag). To check again:
#
#   gh attestation verify check_nsclient-1.2.0-windows-x64.exe \
#     --repo mickem/check_nsclient \
#     --signer-workflow mickem/check_nsclient/.github/workflows/release.yml
#
# One line per architecture, since the release publishes a separate binary
# for each; a missing line fails the build, so adding an architecture cannot
# silently skip verification.

# The Windows binaries, shipped inside the signed MSI and the zip.
check_nsclient-x64      1.2.0   7315de5db5870ed9a6897e012aadc668d84e5924368cb87aeb5fc27872da3ac5
check_nsclient-x86      1.2.0   a8aeed95663b858bc4db3e79140ea4deb9ce5809f3d7e4734f2aff660ee69aca
check_nsclient-arm64    1.2.0   daa7be7174fcebd1b15c7ab78726b303c9c841147ee6b7735d1636126b710987

# The Linux binaries, shipped inside the .deb and .rpm packages and fetched by
# build-debian.yml and build-redhat.yml. Keyed by the `arch` of those
# workflows' matrices.
check_nsclient-linux-x64    1.2.0   c53c70fe35b39940e60db44fe30cf1c7b78972db2e99cd5f2db101e72682f54f
check_nsclient-linux-arm64  1.2.0   ea44ac1dca16befa4207d6b0351b5ce5e0876e5579904d4d7e09fc076ac66cc6

# The release's SHA256SUMS itself. The Windows build fetches the release's
# SBOM for the binary it bundles, checks it against this list, and nests it
# into the NSClient++ SBOM, so the check_nsclient Rust crates are listed too.
check_nsclient-sha256sums   1.2.0   61c6feaa11a07af70a487109a83cc9e03ac68443aa1a764198f5c6de9c5d569f
